posts.t:
Most people use Claude like a search bar.

The people getting real work out of it use Skills: small saved workflows Claude loads by itself when the task comes up.

Same process every time. No re-typing prompts.

A Claude Skill is just one markdown file:

- name
- when to use it
- what to ask you
- numbered steps
- output format
- rules

That's it. No code. Install once, use forever.

I put 6 of my Claude Skills on GitHub, free:

- Anti-AI-slop editor
- Hook writer
- n8n workflow planner
- Cold email writer
- Headline lab
- Idea validator

{repo}

The #1 reason a Claude Skill doesn't trigger:

The description is vague.

Bad: "Helps with marketing"
Good: "Use when the user needs opening lines for posts, or says their posts get no reach"

Write it like a trigger, not a label.

Words that instantly make writing sound like AI:

delve
elevate
unlock
game-changer
"in today's fast-paced world"
"it's not just X, it's Y"

I made a free Claude Skill that strips all of them out.

Stop asking Claude to "write a post".

Ask it to:
1. write 15 hooks across 5 formulas
2. score each one 1-10
3. give you the top 5 with reasons

You'll never post a weak opening line again.

Numbered steps beat paragraphs.

When you write a prompt or a Claude Skill as 1, 2, 3, 4, Claude follows it in order. When you write a paragraph, it improvises.

Small change, very different output.

One line I add to every Claude Skill:

"If inputs are missing, ask at most 3 short questions, then proceed with sensible defaults and state them."

Kills the endless back-and-forth.

You don't need to code to automate your business anymore.

Describe the automation to Claude.
It plans the n8n workflow node by node.
It writes the importable JSON.
It fixes the error when something breaks.

Claude Skills work in 3 places:

- Claude app: upload the zip in Settings > Capabilities
- Claude Code: drop the folder in ~/.claude/skills
- ChatGPT/Gemini: paste the steps into a Custom GPT or Gem

Cold email rule Claude follows for me:

- first line is about THEM
- one-sentence offer
- one proof point
- end with a question, not "book a call"
- under 100 words
- no links in email #1

Reply rates go up. Every time.

Prompt libraries: 500 prompts you copy, paste and forget.

Skills: 12 workers you install once and Claude uses automatically.

I switched and never went back.

Before you build a digital product, make Claude run this:

- painful problem?
- people already paying?
- can you reach them?
- clear format?
- can you ship in 2 weeks?

Then 3 risks + a 48-hour test for each. Go / tweak / drop.

Your bio is a landing page.

who you help + the result + proof + one call to action.

That's the whole formula. Claude can write 5 versions in 10 seconds.

Faceless video workflow with Claude:

1. hook bank (first 3 seconds)
2. 30-60s script with timing
3. shot list
4. AI b-roll prompts
5. captions + on-screen text

You just assemble and post.

threads:
I replaced 40 saved prompts with 12 Claude Skills.

Here's how skills work and how to write one in 20 minutes:

1/ A skill is a folder with one SKILL.md file.

At the top: a name and a description. The description tells Claude WHEN to use it.

2/ Write the description like a trigger:

"Use when the user needs opening lines for posts, threads or emails, or says their posts get no reach."

List the actual phrases people type.

3/ Then the body:

- what to ask the user for
- numbered steps
- output format
- rules (what never to do)
4/ Numbered steps matter. Claude follows 1-2-3 far more reliably than a paragraph.

5/ Add this rule to every skill:

"Ask at most 3 short questions, then proceed with sensible defaults."
6/ Install: Claude app (Settings > Capabilities > upload zip), Claude Code (~/.claude/skills), or paste into ChatGPT/Gemini.

7/ I put 10 free skills + a setup PDF here:

{vault}
How to make AI writing not sound like AI (a checklist I gave Claude):
1/ Ban the tells: delve, elevate, unlock, game-changer, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's not just X, it's Y".
2/ Replace every vague claim with a number, a name or an example.
3/ Vary sentence length. Fragments are fine. Real people write them.
4/ Contractions. Plain verbs. No "utilize".
5/ Cut anything the reader would skim.
6/ Never add facts that weren't there.

7/ I turned this into a free Claude Skill so it runs every time:

{repo}
Build a Gumroad product with Claude in a weekend. The exact steps:
1/ Demand: have Claude list 15 product ideas from real complaints in your niche and score them.
2/ Validate: pain, buyers already paying, reachable audience, clear format, shippable in 2 weeks.
3/ Offer: one promise, components, bonuses, a value anchor.
4/ Build: outline, then one chapter or template at a time.
5/ Price: free lead magnet -> low pack -> deep pack -> bundle.
6/ Page: headline, bullets, FAQ, one call to action.

7/ Every step above is a Claude Skill in my Digital Product Creator pack, or all of them in the full library:

n8n looks scary. With Claude it isn't. How I plan any automation:

1/ Say the goal as: trigger -> steps -> result.
"When someone buys on Gumroad -> add them to my email list -> send a welcome email."
2/ Claude picks the nodes for each step: trigger, apps, logic, AI.
3/ It flags what needs credentials or a paid plan before you start.
4/ It writes the workflow JSON. You import it: Workflows > Import from file.
5/ When it breaks, paste the error. Claude explains it and gives the exact fix.
